clue.text: Tango with nudist surprisingly very good

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of the two words turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A dancer finds a tango partnered by a naturist is remarkably fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' shuffles all eleven letters of TANGO and NUDIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excellent stands out from the rest, so the word is a synonym for very good.

clue.text: One in 100 has competition with worker after 1st of October

indicators.note: after says the rest follows that opening letter
1st of picks the opening letter of the month

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
a cup is a competition, such as the FA Cup
the ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A statistic: one in a hundred enters a contest with a worker after the start of October.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in 100' reads as a ratio, but 'One in' is the definition: the person inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is someone who lives in or occupies a place, a person inside.

clue.text: Inconsequential affair involving three people?

definitions.meaning: read as tri- (three) plus fling, a brief romance

explanation.definitionFit: Trivial matters are of no importance, while a fling involving three is jokingly a tri-fling.

clue.text: Bombs military vehicles

definitions.meaning: fails badly, as a show bombs at the box office

explanation.definitionFit: A flop collapses or fails, and armoured tracked war machines share the same name.

clue.text: Mathematical genius cuddling wife in Basildon, perhaps …

indicators.note: cuddling means the scientist's name wraps its arms round the wife letter

parts.note: Isaac Newton co-invented calculus

explanation.surface: A brilliant mathematician embraces his wife in an Essex town.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a town in Essex, England, built after the Second World War under the New Towns Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Basildon is an example of a planned post-war settlement, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: … to the extent stylish couch warps at the centre

parts.note: in means fashionable
a sofa is a couch

indicators.note: at the centre picks the middle letter of the five-letter word

explanation.surface: A trendy couch has buckled so much it bends in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as far as or to the degree that, the same sense of extent.

clue.text: Sage Derby mixed up with garbage, oddly

indicators.note: mixed up means the letters are jumbled together
oddly picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Sage Derby cheese ends up mixed in with the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is a green-marbled English cheese; 'oddly' takes GRAE from garbage, and 'mixed up' shuffles it with DERBY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise old person, and an old man with a grey beard is a symbol of wisdom.

clue.text: Lubricant left following Love Island

indicators.note: following says the piece for left comes after the other two

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Sounds like reality-TV gossip: sun cream left behind after a stint on Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British reality dating show; here it splits into O for love and I for island.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is the commonest lubricant, used to keep machinery running smoothly.

clue.text: Nothing sounded English in Mandarin?

definitions.note: a noun for a citrus fruit, the question mark flagging an example

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
rang means sounded, as a bell

explanation.surface: A zero seemed to sound like English when spoken in Chinese.
explanation.walkthrough: Mandarin looks like the Chinese language, but it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a type of small citrus fruit, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Large snake is something that can send you in the opposite direction?

definitions.text: something that can send you in the opposite direction?

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: A big snake turns out to send you the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Snakes and Ladders, snakes send you down and ladders up, so this is the opposite of the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: In the board game, climbing one takes you upwards, the reverse of a snake's slide down.

clue.text: International footballer finally stops John Stones

indicators.note: stops means the pieces plug the gap in the lavatory word, as a stopper fills a hole

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a lavatory

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word footballer

explanation.surface: England defender John Stones is held up by an overseas player.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stones is an England footballer, so the surface reads as one name; 'John' and 'Stones' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones piled up as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Heading west, spotted cat about to be ignored by antelope in desert

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the word is read right to left

parts.note: spotted means saw, as in caught sight of

indicators.note: to be ignored says the letters for about are dropped from the animal

parts.note: taken as written
CA, short for circa, means about
an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A wildlife report: a leopard is seen heading west, giving up on an antelope in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading west' turns SAW into WAS; 'about to be ignored' takes CA (circa) from CAT, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasteland is barren, empty country, which is what a desert is.

clue.text: Dispose of language of France

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A linguistic question: what is the language spoken in France?
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something off quickly, food or an opponent, is to get rid of it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Pester the Spanish to return instrument

parts.note: to bug someone is to pester them

indicators.note: to return means the Spanish article is read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone nags a Spaniard to give back a borrowed musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a brass wind instrument used for military calls.

clue.text: Target revolutionary characters from Mani peninsula

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
characters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Insurgents on the Mani peninsula in Greece are singled out as a target.
explanation.definitionFit: In skittles each pin is what the bowler aims to knock down, so it is a target.

clue.text: Child welfare agency to reimburse about 50 grand, initially recompensing overworked, underpaid parents

indicators.note: about says the pay word goes round the numeral

parts.note: to pay back is to reimburse
L is the Roman numeral for 50
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A care body offering roughly fifty thousand to compensate overstretched parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgroup is an informal pre-school where young children are looked after, a loose welfare service.

clue.text: Bishop leaves money for study

indicators.note: leaves says the bishop letter departs from the money word

parts.note: bread is slang for money
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric walks away from the money in order to study.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university means to study it.

clue.text: Official policies on staff

parts.note: party lines are policies
to man is to staff, as a desk is manned

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat's rules about staffing levels.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant referee in football is a match official who signals offside and throw-ins.

clue.text: Admitted 'Roll with it' upset square journalist

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: S is short for square, as in street names
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: An editor confesses that the Oasis song 'Roll With It' upset a stuffy reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll With It' is an Oasis song; BAP is a British bread roll and 'upset' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening someone admits them into the Church as a member.

clue.text: Spa town hit hard

parts.note: to bat is to hit with a bat
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A resort town is struck badly, by recession or storm.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman hot springs and baths.

clue.text: Unkind prostitute's device for getting leg over?

parts.note: ho is slang for a prostitute; the 's attaches the next piece
a stile is a step for climbing over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A saucy innuendo about a sex worker's aid for getting her leg over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your leg over' is British slang for sex; here it is literal: a stile lets walkers step over a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means unfriendly or aggressive, a synonym for unkind.

clue.text: Composed by Gershwin: Islands in the Stream?

indicators.note: by puts the lyricist's name beside the word for composed

parts.note: composed means made, as music is made
Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George Gershwin

explanation.surface: A pub-quiz claim that Gershwin wrote the country hit 'Islands in the Stream'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Islands in the Stream' was a Dolly Parton and Kenny Rogers hit; the definition reads it as Atlantic islands in the ocean current.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese archipelago in the Atlantic, lying in the waters of the Canary Current, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Trough enthrals area supervisor

indicators.note: enthrals is read as holds within, so the trough wraps the area letter

parts.note: a manger is a feeding trough

explanation.surface: A captivating feeding trough holds a boss's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss oversees staff, so the word is a synonym for supervisor.

clue.text: Meat fried in breadcrumbs? Look out! Run away!

indicators.note: out means the look word is taken out

parts.note: an escalope is a thin slice of meat, often breaded and fried
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A frantic kitchen warning: hot breaded meat, watch out, flee!
explanation.definitionFit: To flee or break free is to get away, an imperative synonym.

clue.text: Pathetic leading idiot overthrown

indicators.note: in a down clue, overthrown means turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: top means leading, as in top of the league
nit is slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A sorry tale of a foolish leader who has been ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot means shoddy and inferior, as in a tinpot dictator, so pathetic.

clue.text: Cast or harness for broken arm

definitions.meaning: a loop of cloth supporting an injured arm from the neck

explanation.definitionFit: To fling is to throw, and the cloth support for an injured limb shares the same word.

clue.text: 'Feeling is feeling', male admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the male letter is let inside the adjective

parts.note: sentient means able to feel

explanation.surface: A man confesses the tautology that feeling is feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Feeling' is a noun (the definition), the second an adjective, SENTIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an emotion or attitude, so it is a synonym of a feeling.

clue.text: Home help lifted nation

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the word is raised to read upwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: A domestic helper has been stolen from a country.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country in South Asia, a nation.

clue.text: Favourable introduction to Austin Powers' gallivanting

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: P stands for power, and doubling a letter makes a plural abbreviation, as pp for pages
gallivanting means roving about in search of fun

explanation.surface: A film critic gives a warm review of Austin Powers' womanising escapades.
explanation.walkthrough: Austin Powers is a film spy; split here into A from the start of Austin and PP for powers.
explanation.definitionFit: An approving response shows favour or agreement, so it is synonymous with being favourable.

clue.text: Around 0.5d = $0.10n (n>1)

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: half detached, read as semi-d, a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A mock equation converting old halfpennies into several American ten-cent coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 0.5d looks like old British money, half a penny, but means semi-detached house, SEMI-D, read backwards; $0.10 is a ten-cent coin and n>1 makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A US ten-cent coin is a dime, and n of them with n above one are plural coins.

clue.text: Leather covers put away

indicators.note: covers says the word leather wraps round the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Leather covers are stored away somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an idiom meaning to consume it.

clue.text: Badly need air-drop to be determined beforehand

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are poorly arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: A relief air-drop is urgently needed and must be planned in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fated or decided in advance has been settled before it happens.
